extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art/architecture, architectural historians, practicing architects interested in Venetian Gothic/Renaissance design
extracted.subtask_description: Close critical analysis of the design, history, and decorative principles of the Ducal Palace (Palazzo Ducale) in Venice, with attention to placement of openings, sculptural program, and the choice between repair and rebuilding. Useful for evaluating or designing historic civic architecture and its ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce light in simple masses rather than many broken streams
rubrics_metrics.description: The ceiling of the new room was to be adorned by paintings of the best masters and it became important to raise the light near that roof and keep the tone of illumination in the Council Chamber serene; therefore to introduce light rather in simple masses than in many broken streams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design fenestration and lighting to produce broad, unified illumination suitable for viewing large ceiling paintings and for maintaining a calm overall lighting tone; avoid many small, fragmented light sources that break up the illumination and distract from painted ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place windows with reference to interior function, not external symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The old Venetian raised the large windows to their proper position with reference to the interior of the chamber, and suffered the external appearance to take care of itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize internal requirements (lighting, viewing of artworks, comfort of occupants) over maintaining strict external symmetry. Be willing to alter the façade if it better serves interior harmony and function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor paintings and civic comfort above architect's external reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The old Venetian thought of the honor of the paintings, and the comfort of the senate, before his own reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning or altering civic interiors, place the needs of artworks' display and the users' comfort above concerns about preserving the architect's external compositional reputation or façade regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation in wall spaces (above and below windows) can enhance the building's effect
rubrics_metrics.description: I believe the whole pile rather gains than loses in effect by the variation thus obtained in the spaces of wall above and below the windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate asymmetry or variation in the spacing and proportions around openings may produce a more interesting and effective façade than rigidly uniform treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corners/angles of nearly square buildings should be enriched and softened by sculpture
rubrics_metrics.description: As the building was very nearly square on the ground plan, a peculiar prominence and importance were given to its angles, which rendered it necessary that they should be enriched and softened by sculpture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bare sharp angles on square or blocky buildings; use sculptural groups, buttresses, turrets, niches, or other decorations at corners to relieve harshness and increase refinement of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break the angle (a peculiarly Gothic principle) for structural and aesthetic reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: This principle of breaking the angle is peculiarly Gothic, arising partly out of the necessity of strengthening the flanks of enormous buildings ... partly out of the natural dislike of the meagreness of effect in buildings which admitted large surfaces of wall, if the angle were entirely unrelieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structural devices (buttresses, pinnacles, turrets) or sculptural articulation at corners both to strengthen building flanks and to avoid visual meagreness where large wall surfaces meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural program should occupy corner-stones to express the builder's purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: These [corner sculptures] are the very corner stones of the edifice, and in them we may expect to find the most important evidences of the feeling, as well as of the skill, of the builder. If he has anything to say to us of the purpose with which he built the palace, it is sure to be said here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select subjects for large corner sculptures that communicate civic values, intentions, or identity; the iconography at corners should be legible and meaningful because it is highly prominent and symbolic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange angle sculpture in a hierarchical sequence from ground to roof
rubrics_metrics.description: The pillars of the two bearing arcades are much enlarged in thickness at the angles, and their capitals increased in depth, breadth, and fulness of subject; above each capital, on the angle of the wall, a sculptural subject is introduced, consisting, in the great lower arcade, of two or more figures of the size of life; in the upper arcade, of a single angel holding a scroll: above these angels rise the twisted pillars with their crowning niches, thus forming an unbroken line of decoration from the ground to the top of the angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a continuous, ordered vertical program at angles: enlarged supporting columns and enriched capitals at base; large figure groups in lower arcade; single angelic or emblematic figures in upper arcade; then spiral shafts and niches—creating an integrated upward-reading decorative scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a single lofty room is desired, give it the entire height rather than dividing it
rubrics_metrics.description: When a room was wanted, there was no need to divide the added portion into two stories. The entire height was given to the single chamber, being indeed not too great for just harmony with its enormous length and breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large ceremonial or council chambers, prefer a single tall volume to multiple stories to achieve harmonious proportions with great length and breadth; height contributes to dignity and appropriate space for ceiling decoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide repair vs rebuilding by weighing safety, costs, tradition, and civic honor
rubrics_metrics.description: It was debated ... whether the ruin should not be thrown down, and an entirely new palace built in its stead. The opinions of all the leading architects of Venice were taken, respecting the safety of the walls, or the possibility of repairing them as they stood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contemplating restoration after disaster, consult expert structural opinions, consider historical value and civic honor, evaluate treasury constraints, and weigh long-term cultural cost of rebuilding older fabric versus replacing with new design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide humane, ventilated prison accommodations rather than relying on mythic depictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of being, as usually reported, small furnaces under the leads of the palace, they [the 'piombi'] were comfortable rooms, with good flat roofs of larch, and carefully ventilated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutional or penal spaces to be humane and ventilated; resist sensational or traditional myths about cramped, unhealthy conditions—ensure functional, well-ventilated rooms if prisons are part of the complex.
